the electronic spectrum of a hexagon is determined by a combination of the $C_6$ symmetry and time reversal.

the $C_6$ symmetry group is the main responsible for the electronic spectrum of benzene and that the electronic spectrum of borazine is the result of the interplay between $C_3$, $C_2$ and $C_1$ symmetry groups.

(i) the electronic structure of a ring can be understood with a simple tight binding model, (ii) the electronic spectrum of a ring is described by two doublets, (iii) the degeneracy lifts of the doublets are due to the breaking of $C_3$, conjugation and time reversal symmetries and (iv) a supersymmetry exists in the electronic spectrum of $C_6$.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the electronic spectrum of a hexagon.
the electronic properties of a hexagonal lattice.
the study of the electronic structure of molecules and solids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electronic structure of a $6$-membered ring, with or without conjugation symmetry breaking, is determined by a combination of $C_3$, time reversal and magnetic field symmetries, and the presence of defects.
the electronic spectra are not a consequence of aromaticity but rather the result of symmetry breaking and the introduction of defects in a ring structure.
the electronic spectrum of the hexagonal ring is determined by a combination of $C_3$, conjugation and time reversal symmetry breaking mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic spectrum of a hexagon can be understood in terms of the $C_6$ symmetry group, together with a magnetic field and the presence of defects.
a hexagonal ring with $C_3\otimes T$ symmetry has $2$ doublets, while a hexagonal ring without $C_3 \otimes T$ has $4$ doublets.

we have shown that electronic spectra can be analysed with the help of group theoretical methods and that the inclusion of defects in the ring can be used to lift degeneracies and induce new electronic states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic spectra of hexagonal rings are determined by the $C_6$ and $C_3v$ groups.

a tight binding approach with first, second, third and fourth neighbours, together with the $C_{6v}$ group and time reversal, provides a simple and elegant description of the electronic spectrum of a $6$ hexagonal ring.
the electronic structure of the hexagonal ring, and of the benzene molecule, can be explained with a simple model.
